Strait of Hormuz Status: October 9, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  222 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
9 October 2026 .
Brent $ 103.97 + 2.03 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 gCaptain and MarineLink report Iran has vowed to block more Hormuz routes, raising attack risks for tankers.

02 The U.S. sanctioned 22 tankers and dozens of individuals linked to Iran's oil trade, per gCaptain.

03 Brent stood at $103.97, up 2.03% over 24 hours, as of 00:19 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, and the operational picture darkened further when gCaptain and MarineLink reported that Iran has vowed to block additional routes it considers unauthorized, raising attack risks for tankers transiting the waterway. gCaptain and BNN Bloomberg report that Trump is readying new Iran strikes as Hormuz attacks ramp up, while gCaptain and BNN Bloomberg also report that Iran will soon close routes it has not authorized. Reuters reports that Hormuz traffic has fallen to its lowest level in over two months following recent attacks. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent crude stood at $103.97, up 2.03% over 24 hours, as of 00:19 UTC; WTI was at $91.21. On the sanctions front, gCaptain reports the United States imposed sanctions on 22 tankers and dozens of individuals and companies linked to Iran's oil trade. Democracy Now! reports a tanker was struck north of Qatar after Iran warned ships against bypassing what it calls the Hormuz blockade; the Acers, reported by BBC News as hit by multiple projectiles in the Gulf off Qatar with casualties aboard, is a carried-over incident first reported on October 8. An attack on a merchant vessel reported on October 7 left 11 Indian crew injured, per earlier reporting. gCaptain separately reports that Saudi Arabia is in talks to formalize Hormuz shuttle arrangements to compete for market share displaced by the crisis. As of 00:20 UTC, 206 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
